clue.text: Defaces most of fridge taking issue with repair

indicators.note: something under repair is being put back together differently, so the letters are reordered
most of the word fridge is used, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone damages the fridge while sorting out a problem with its repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' cuts FRIDGE to FRIDG; 'with repair' then shuffles FRIDG and ISSUE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for spoiling the look of something: to deface is to mar its appearance.

clue.text: Endless learning in pale Italian city

indicators.note: the shortened word sits inside the fence

parts.note: a pale is a fence of stakes

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the synonym goes

parts.note: lore is traditional learning or knowledge

explanation.surface: A pale scholar endlessly studying in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pale' looks like an adjective but is the noun meaning a fence; 'Endless' trims LORE to LOR, which goes 'in' FENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is the Tuscan capital, a real example of a city in Italy.

clue.text: Rising cricketers to make attempt

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: bats is a crossword term for batsmen, the cricketers who bat

explanation.surface: Up-and-coming cricketers setting out to have a go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns BATS upside down in this down light, giving the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stab is an informal word for a try, as in having a go at something.

clue.text: Hypothetical proposition picked up blemishes lots made less of

indicators.note: lifted up in a down light, so this word is read upwards

parts.note: warts are skin blemishes

indicators.note: the word is reduced, losing its last letter

parts.note: many means lots

explanation.surface: A theory overheard about skin flaws being played down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like a sound signal but here reverses WARTS to STRAW in the down light; 'made less of' trims MANY to MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw man is a weak argument set up only to be knocked down, a hypothetical proposition in debate.

clue.text: Nurse assigned to body tissue

parts.note: to nurse is to tend
on, as in being on a team or rota, means assigned to it

explanation.surface: A nurse allocated to work on a patient's tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon is the fibrous tissue joining muscle to bone, a kind of body tissue.

clue.text: First to last in contest? That's horrible

indicators.note: that letter goes inside the synonym for contest

parts.note: to vie is to contest or compete

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word last is used

explanation.surface: Going from first to last in a race: what a dreadful result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First to last' reads as a race result, but it means the first letter of 'last', L, which goes 'in' VIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Vile and horrible are synonyms for something extremely unpleasant.

clue.text: Last of heated wax a source of risk

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word heated is taken

parts.note: a wax is an old word for a fit of anger

explanation.surface: The last of some hot wax poses a hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wax' looks like the candle material, but in older British usage a wax is a temper, a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A danger is something that may cause harm, which is a source of risk.

clue.text: Party victory, but one unseated is unhappy

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: removed from its place, so this letter is taken out

parts.note: a win is a victory
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A party wins an election, but a member who loses a seat is glum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one unseated' reads as a defeated MP; it means I is removed from WIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down is an idiom for being low in spirits, sad or depressed.

clue.text: One positioned around Lake? On the contrary, as it happens

definitions.text: One positioned around Lake? On the contrary, as it happens

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the letters for one positioned go around the lake's letter

parts.note: set means placed or positioned

explanation.surface: A thing placed around a lake? No, the reverse is true.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay puts I SET around L; 'On the contrary' points out that in reality the lake surrounds the little island, and 'as it happens' says the letters still work.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a small island, something with water all round it rather than placed around water.

clue.text: Those people stir about backing King & I or an operetta

parts.note: them refers to those people

indicators.note: going backwards, so these two letters are read in reverse

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
an ado is a fuss or stir about something

explanation.surface: Those people make a fuss over staging The King and I or another stage work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King & I' looks like the musical title, but it supplies K and I, which 'backing' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado is a comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, so an example of an operetta.

clue.text: Hothead provided, while backing away, attempt to get new style

indicators.note: moving backwards, so the two letters are read in reverse

parts.note: if means provided, on condition that
to rebrand is to try to give something a new image or style

explanation.surface: A hothead, backing off, tries for a fresh look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'while backing away' turns IF into FI.
explanation.definitionFit: A firebrand is a passionate, impetuous agitator, a hothead in the figurative sense.

clue.text: River twisting back round grand Scottish town

indicators.note: the reversed river goes round this letter
turning back, so the river's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river
G is short for grand, slang for a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A river winding back round a grand Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisting back' reverses NILE to ELIN, which goes 'round' G.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgin is a historic town in Moray, in the north-east of Scotland.

clue.text: Guard talent manager confused by address to female

indicators.note: mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Ms is a title used in addressing a woman

explanation.surface: An agent left bewildered by how to address a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' shuffles the letters of 'talent manager'; 'address to female' is the courtesy title, not a speech. The guard is one of the British royal bodyguard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gentlemen-at-Arms are the sovereign's ceremonial bodyguard in Britain, so one is a royal guard.

clue.text: Romance, I note, means extra time in bed

parts.note: to romance is to tell fanciful stories, to lie

explanation.surface: A romance, I note, means staying longer under the covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romance' is a verb here: to romance is to invent tall tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-in is a British idiom for staying in bed later than usual in the morning.

clue.text: Sycophant now making a switch

indicators.note: two letters change places, so one letter shifts its position

parts.note: today means at the present time, now

explanation.surface: A flatterer who is now changing sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a switch' swaps the A and D of TODAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady is a fawning flatterer, a synonym for a sycophant.

clue.text: Siren, say, good over emotional pressure applied to young man

indicators.note: the following pieces are attached after the young man
in a down light the letter for good sits above the pressure

parts.note: a son is a young male child
stress is mental or emotional strain

explanation.surface: Good advice about stress offered to a young lad.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'over' means placed above, and 'applied to' attaches the rest beneath the young man; 'Siren' is a singer here, not an alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a seductive singer of myth, so an example of a female singer, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Eggs academic official to take care of girls' school

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
a dean is a senior university official

explanation.surface: A university official's eggs placed in charge of a school for girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Roedean is a famous independent boarding school for girls near Brighton, England.

clue.text: Dodge recalling response expressing preference for investment over expenditure?

indicators.note: calling back, so the reply is read in reverse

parts.words: response expressing preference for investment over expenditure
parts.note: a person preferring to invest rather than spend might say no, I save

explanation.surface: Avoiding a spending question by recalling an answer about preferring investment.
explanation.walkthrough: The long phrase is the spoken reply NO I SAVE; 'recalling' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasion is avoidance, the act of dodging a question or duty.

clue.text: Golden city rebuilt centre of golden road

indicators.note: constructed again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged
the word golden loses its outer letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: A legendary golden city reconstructed around a golden road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes OLDE from GOLDEN; 'rebuilt' mixes it with ROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado was the legendary South American city of gold sought by explorers.

clue.text: Hostile in one examination of a person, suppressing editor

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: holding down, so the editor's letters are removed

parts.note: a medical is a physical examination

explanation.surface: An editor gagged during a hostile physical check-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressing editor' removes ED from MEDICAL, leaving MICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Inimical means unfriendly or harmful, a synonym for hostile.

clue.text: Representation of dandy evilnesses?

indicators.note: a fresh presentation of these letters means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A depiction of a fop's wicked traits.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and anagram: the letters of DANDY EVILNESSES rearranged describe the sins, which are evils such as a dandy's vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: The seven deadly sins are the cardinal vices of Christian teaching, so the classic list of evils.

clue.text: John picked up curious line in path of river

indicators.note: lifted in a down light, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, a lav
a ley line is a supposed mysterious alignment of ancient sites

explanation.surface: John heard of a strange line along a river's course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' reverses LAV to VAL in this down light, not a sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A valley is the low ground a river runs through, the course it carves.

clue.text: Festival's energy's mostly towards the end?

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: most of the word is used, losing its final letter

parts.note: astern means towards the rear or back end of a ship

explanation.surface: Does a festival's energy mainly come at the end?
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims ASTERN to ASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian feast celebrating the resurrection, a major festival.

clue.text: Recalled demand to have brought in one flower

indicators.note: the reversed word takes this letter inside it
called back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a call is a demand, as in a call for action
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone remembers being asked to bring in a single flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' reverses CALL to LLAC, which brings I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a shrub with fragrant purple or white blossom, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Missed opening, moving second to third

indicators.note: the letter is taken out and shifted elsewhere
its new place is the third position in the word

parts.note: a slot is a narrow opening

explanation.surface: A missed chance, with the runner-up shifting to third place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' looks like a race place but is S, which shifts to third place in SLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lost can mean failed to catch or take, as a missed chance is a lost one.

clue.text: Republican beset by economy, in brief

indicators.note: surrounded by, so the letter sits inside the saving

parts.note: a cut is an economy, a saving

explanation.surface: A Republican hemmed in by spending cuts, in short.
explanation.definitionFit: Curt describes speech that is short and abrupt, close in sense to brief.

clue.text: Carries on about heartless woman, though with less substance

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the woman's outer letters
carries on suggests wild behaviour, so the word carries is rearranged
the middle of the word woman is removed, keeping its outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone rants about a cold woman, though the argument is thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carries on' reads as ranting; 'on' scrambles CARRIES into SCRAIER, which goes 'about' WN, the ends of 'woman'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrawnier is the comparative of scrawny, meaning thinner and bonier, having less flesh.

clue.text: What initially remains in the laundry?

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word what is taken

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A question about what is left behind in the laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: ash is the remains of a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: The wash is a name for clothes being laundered, as in 'it's in the wash'.

clue.text: Hurried round region containing hot lead

indicators.note: the hurried word goes round the whole region

parts.note: sped means hurried

indicators.note: the region holds this letter inside it

parts.note: an area is a region
H is short for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone rushed round an area with a hot lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' is a verb here, to go in front, not the metal; 'containing' and 'round' nest one container inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: To spearhead is to lead an attack or campaign from the front.

clue.text: One abandoning flight's heavenly view

indicators.note: leaving behind, so this letter is removed

parts.note: a flight is a set of stairs
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone abandoning a flight to gaze at the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks like air travel, but it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Stars fill the night sky, a view of the heavens.
